assessment: In their important study, Gicking et al., study the physical properties of artificial complexes composed of the dynein-dynactin-BicD2 (DDB) complex linked to one of three classes of kinesins (1, 2, or 3) via a DNA scaffold. They find that all three kinesins can move to the plus-end of microtubules when coupled to the DDB complex. This is surprising because motors in the kinesin-2 and kinesin-3 families have been shown to have a higher load sensitivity; however, the authors show that the faster reattachment kinetics of these motors compensate for their faster detachment rates under load. This work is compelling and relevant to both the biophysics and the neuroscience fields.
